KEEPING THE ADVENTURE OPEN. ✈️🏕️

A great fly-in destination needs more than airplanes. It needs people willing to look after the ground beneath them.

A November 7 General Aviation News report highlights work at Arizona’s Grapevine Airstrip, near Roosevelt Lake. The Recreational Aviation Foundation confirms that runway crack sealing was completed in September after weather delays.

The Arizona Pilots Association covered most of the sealing cost, with the U.S. Forest Service contributing through an RAF-arranged cost-share agreement. Contractors handled the sealing, while volunteers help maintain the camping facilities and tackle weeds and erosion.

That teamwork helps keep a special kind of general aviation adventure possible: fly in, pitch a tent and spend time with other people who love to fly.

Here’s to the pilots, volunteers and partners who care for these places long after the engines shut down. 💛

Sources: General Aviation News, November 7, 2026; Recreational Aviation Foundation, October 29, 2026.
